title: Ready for AI at work?
description: Test your judgment on drafts, workflows, and human review.

questions.question: AI invents a deadline in meeting notes. What should you do?
options: Keep it because it seems reasonable
Check the source and mark a missing date as unconfirmed
Ask AI to invent a more convenient date
questions.explanation: Meeting summaries must preserve actual commitments. Missing details should be visible.

questions.question: What should a pilot measure?
options: Only how many people opened the tool
Only how attractive the demo looked
Quality, correction effort, usefulness, and total time
questions.explanation: A pilot should assess the whole workflow and its value, including review and correction.

questions.question: Which automation needs a stronger review checkpoint?
options: An action that sends a binding quote to a customer
questions.explanation: External commitments and consequential actions need controls proportionate to their impact.

questions.question: When should failure handling be tested?
options: Never if the first demo succeeds
questions.explanation: Missing inputs, duplicates, service failures, and recovery need testing before reliance.

questions.question: Does every automation need AI?
options: Yes, automation and AI are identical
No, stable rules may solve the task more simply
Only if it uses a spreadsheet
questions.explanation: Many repeatable tasks are better handled by conventional rules. Use AI when its flexibility adds value.

questions.question: What should you do with an AI-generated spreadsheet formula?
options: Use it because formulas cannot be wrong
Test expected values and edge cases
Check only whether it fits in the cell
questions.explanation: Test formulas against known results and cases such as blanks, duplicates, and different formats.
